newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan hijacker sentenced to eight years jail.
newsitem.headline: Japan hijacker sentenced to eight years jail.

text.p: A man upset over the gas attack on Tokyo's subway system was sentenced to eight years in prison on Friday for hijacking a jumbo jet on a domestic flight in 1995.
Fumio Kutsumi, 55, commandeered the All Nippon Airways (ANA) Boeing 747 on a flight bound for the northern Japanese city of Hakodate on the island of Hokkaido from Tokyo on June 21, 1995.
Kutsumi held 365 passengers and crew hostage for 16 hours before police raided the plane at dawn the following morning.

Kutsumi claimed to be a member of Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect), the doomsday cult accused of the March 20, 1995 sarin nerve gas attack on Tokyo's subway that killed 12 people and made thousands ill.
He said he was carrying sarin and demanded to meet Shoko Asahara, the cult leader now on trial for murder in the subway attack.
In sentencing Kutsumi, Hakodate District Court Presiding Judge Hideaki Arakawa dismissed arguments by Kutsumi's lawyers that the defendant was mentally ill or depressed.
But the judge also rejected prosecution demands for a 15-year prison term on the grounds that Kutsumi did not actually use guns or bombs and he later "seriously reflected" on what he had done.
In the trial, Kutsumi had said he wanted to meet Asahara to make the cult leader confess to the subway attack.
No one was seriously injured in the hijacking.
